title: Put each change in the least persistent layer
description: Choose a product requirement and an adaptation mechanism. The workbench shows where state lives, how quickly it can change, and what must be released or rolled back.
notice: These values are a teaching model, not vendor benchmarks. The decision invariant is to use the smallest reversible mechanism that satisfies capability and freshness needs.

methods.label: Prompt and examples
methods.detail: Place temporary instructions and demonstrations in the current request.
methods.contract: Version the prompt, bound its token budget, and evaluate the full request template.
methods.failureMode: Instructions compete with user input or disappear when context is truncated.

methods.label: Retrieval grounding
methods.detail: Fetch authorized evidence at request time and keep source identity outside model weights.
methods.contract: Measure retrieval recall, access control, citation support, freshness, and empty-result behavior.
methods.failureMode: The generator answers from weak or unauthorized evidence, or no useful evidence is retrieved.

methods.label: Supervised adapter
methods.detail: Train a bounded behavior or domain pattern while preserving a separately versioned base model.
methods.contract: Trace training data, compare against prompt and retrieval baselines, and pin adapter plus base versions.
methods.failureMode: The adapter memorizes artifacts, regresses general behavior, or becomes incompatible with a new base.

methods.label: Preference-tuned checkpoint
methods.detail: Change broad response behavior from ranked or scored outputs under a release process.
methods.contract: Audit preference collection, evaluator agreement, reward misspecification, regressions, and rollback.
methods.failureMode: The learned objective rewards a proxy that does not match user intent on important slices.

scenarios.label: A temporary answer format
scenarios.brief: A workflow needs concise JSON for this request path and may change next week.
scenarios.consequence: A request template is visible and reversible; training weights would make a short-lived contract unnecessarily persistent.

scenarios.label: A policy corpus changes hourly
scenarios.brief: Answers must use current authorized policy text and show the supporting source.
scenarios.consequence: Retrieval keeps volatile facts and permissions outside weights, where updates and revocation can happen independently.

scenarios.label: A stable domain protocol
scenarios.brief: Prompt and retrieval baselines still fail a versioned transformation protocol.
scenarios.consequence: A bounded adapter may justify its training and release burden after lighter mechanisms fail on representative cases.

scenarios.label: Broad response preferences
scenarios.brief: The product has audited comparisons of helpful and unhelpful responses across many tasks.
scenarios.consequence: Preference tuning changes general behavior, so the evidence and regression surface must be broad enough to justify a new checkpoint.
